title: Seva as spirituality
hook: service is not a side activity; it is the path

segments.voice: Yesterday, miri and piri: two swords, two buildings facing, one life. Your line: both together.

At a gurdwara door, you take off your shoes. Someone behind a counter takes them, slides them onto a rack, and hands you a token. When you come out, they find your pair and hand it back, sometimes wiped clean. You met that counter on day eight. Who's behind it? Nobody you hired. A college student, a retired engineer, a shopkeeper on his day off, a grandmother who has done it for years. Not paid, not there to be noticed, handling strangers' shoes, and content to be there. Today asks why that counter sits close to the center of Sikh spiritual life.
screen: `SHOES AT THE DOOR.` → `WHO IS BEHIND THE COUNTER?` → `NOT PAID. CONTENT TO BE THERE.`

segments.voice: Seva is selfless service: work done for others with no wage and no score kept. In a gurdwara it looks like cooking and serving in the langar, washing dishes, sweeping floors, minding shoes. Outside, it's anything done for someone who needs it. In Sri Raag, Guru Nanak puts it plainly. In paraphrase: earn service here in the world, and you'll be given a seat in the Lord's court. Notice where the service happens: in the world. Not after. Not somewhere holier. Here, at the shoe counter, at the stove. Tradition tells a story. During a battle, a Sikh named Bhai Ghanaiya went across the field with a water skin, giving water to the wounded, including soldiers from the other side. Some Sikhs complained to Guru Gobind Singh. When the Guru asked him why, tradition says, Ghanaiya answered that he saw no enemy, only the Guru's face in everyone. And the Guru gave him ointment as well, so he could dress their wounds too. Why is seva the path and not a side activity? It works on the very thing we met a few days ago: haumai, ego. It's hard to hold onto I, me, mine while you're scrubbing someone else's pot. So seva isn't a break from prayer. Sikhs speak of it as a form of prayer: the hands remembering what the lips say. The hope is service without the self in the way: no photo, no thank-you required. Service is the path.
screen: `SEVA: SERVICE, NO WAGE, NO SCORE.` · `EARN SERVICE HERE, IN THE WORLD.` · `BHAI GHANAIYA'S WATER SKIN.` · `HANDS THAT LOOSEN HAUMAI.` · then, large: `SERVICE IS THE PATH.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one small act of service nobody would ever thank you for, a dish in the sink, a neighbor's bin, a message to someone who is struggling, and picture doing it slowly, with care, the way someone at the counter hands back a stranger's shoes. Notice any part of you that wants credit, and let it rest. If you pray, offer the act quietly with Waheguru.
Seva as spirituality. Selfless service, done in the world, not beside the path but as the path itself. Today's word.
Your line: service is the path. The hands remember what the lips say. Rest well.

howItsDone: Sikhs do seva in gurdwaras by cooking and serving langar, washing dishes, cleaning and minding shoes, and outside them through volunteer service, understood as a spiritual practice rather than a side activity.

It's a punishment given to members who have broken a gurdwara rule.
